bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: A Practical Guide

Understanding how your hourly wage translates into an annual salary is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your finances. Whether you are on the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) or earning above average, the basic formula remains the same: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year.

### The Standard Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a casual employee working 20 hours per week would use 20 instead of 38. The result is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. So fortnightly = (hourly × hours per week) × 2. This can help you match your budget to your pay cycle.

## Understanding Different Pay Rates

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most industries have award rates set by the Fair Work Commission, which are often higher. Always check the relevant award for your job. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the correct rate.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). When using our timesheet calculator, enter your base hourly rate and tick the casual loading checkbox – we add the 25% automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.** For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 (as per the National Minimum Wage).

### Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). Super is not deducted from your pay; your employer adds it separately. For an annual salary of $60,000, super would be an additional $7,200. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate your tax and Medicare levy. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Low-income earners may be eligible for a reduction or exemption, but the thresholds for 2026–27 have not been confirmed; we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for estimation purposes. The levy applies to most taxpayers.

### Example Calculation

Suppose you earn $40 per hour for a 38-hour week. Annual gross = $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040.

- Tax: $18,200 tax-free, then $26,800 taxed at 15% = $4,020, then remaining $34,040 taxed at 30% = $10,212. Total tax = $14,232.
- Medicare levy: 2% of $79,040 = $1,580.80.
- Net pay after tax and Medicare: $79,040 – $14,232 – $1,580.80 = $63,227.20.
- Super (12% on top): $79,040 × 12% = $9,484.80.

This is an estimate; actual tax may vary based on deductions, offsets, and other factors.

## Salary Packaging Options Australia

If you are exploring [salary packaging options australia](/topics/super-and-packaging), remember that salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) allows you to pay for certain benefits (like a car, laptop, or additional super) with pre-tax dollars. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower both your income tax and Medicare levy. However, salary packaging is not deducted in our basic calculator. Always consult a tax professional or your employer’s salary packaging provider to understand how it affects your take-home pay.

## Average Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week (approx. $108,352 per year). All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week (approx. $82,118 per year). These are **averages**, not medians, and may not reflect your specific job or industry. For more detailed data, see our [reference tables](/data).

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a personalised calculation, use our [timesheet](/).
